description:
FILED s536 (the reviewing session, 2026-11-08) while attributing the round board's MISMATCH *PLAN* rows (blessed `ran 8 of 1008, rc 2`, the board on MAIN-READY-74 read `ran 1 of 1008, rc 1`).

MEASURED (one-file `tools/run-dist-t.pl --rows ~/.cpan/build/IO-Compress-2.214-0 t/105oneshot-deflate.t`, logs ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s536/round/bis/old.log io.log):
  cc5f6310 (-63) 1 row; 157f7255 (-65) 1; 7a4cbf67 (-67) 8, 8, 8; b3d5df1f (-69) 8; 458c4785 (-70) 1, 1, then 8 (a direct run); 4748a7f5 (-71) 1, then 8, 8; fcfcb5d3 (-74) 1 (board and serial re-run).  The SAME extraction flips -> not a code bisect.
Even in an 8-row run the load prints `While evaluating the form starting at line 98 ...: NO!!!!` and the recovery loader continues.

THE DIE: t/compress/CompTestUtils.pm package LexFile, `sub new { foreach () { Carp::croak "NO!!!!" if defined $_; $_ = "tst" . $$ . "X" . $index++ . ".tmp" unless defined $_; } ... }`, called as `my $lex = LexFile->new( my $name );` -- the callee WRITES its argument through the foreach alias of @_ and the caller reads $name back.  A `my $name` declared in the argument list must arrive UNDEF every time; here it arrives defined -- candidates: (a) the declared-in-an-argument `my` is not a fresh cell per execution (a shared cell keeps the previous call's file name -- #4544's family, a `my` in an expression position); (b) the write-back through `foreach (@_)` into a declared-in-argument `my` (#4622 is the assignment-argument twin); the run-to-run flip suggests the cold vs warm module path (the first run of a program builds its compiled file -- #2702) or the order the .pl helpers load in.
CHEAP DISCRIMINATOR: a standalone program `package L; sub new { foreach (@_) { die "NO" if defined $_; $_ = "x" } bless [@_] } package main; for (1..3) { my $l = L->new(my $n); print "$n\n" }` run cold and warm (rm the module cache between) vs perl.
ROWS: the four 105oneshot *PLAN* rows of baselines/cpan-board14-fails.tsv stay blessed as `ran 8 of 1008` (the state most runs give); a run that reads `ran 1` is this task.


=== DONE (s536d) ===
TWO causes, one fixed, one filed (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08).
(1) THE CELL = #3493 (FIXED): oneshot.pl:85 `{ my $lex1 = LexFile->new( my $in ); … }` inside a sub that declared `$in` earlier (`$in = ''` by then) -- both embedded-`my` arms filtered out a name already in `_let_bound_vars`, so the inner `my $in` declared NOTHING and LexFile received the OUTER, defined `$in`: "NO!!!!".  The filter is gone (the declaration arm's re-entry is guarded by the statement, `_emb_let_open`); a statement that also READS the outer name keeps the outer (`_stmt_mentions_again`, residue #4642).  The cheap discriminator (a standalone `L->new(my $n)` loop) was right on base -- the bug needs the OUTER same-name lexical.
(2) THE FLIP = #4643 (FILED, pre-existing): five one-file runs of t/105oneshot-deflate.t on the tree read HEAP, HEAP, 971/37, HEAP, 971/37 -- "Heap exhausted, game over" in SB-REGALLOC compiling oneshot.pl's one giant `sub run`, loaded UNCACHED every run.  No run printed "NO!!!!"; both complete runs gave the same 1008 rows (pass=971 fail=37; the failures are the file's known causes: the croak location `\s+at` NS:ns-error-location, #330 read-only).  The brief's bar "the same row count every time" is NOT met, and cannot be by this batch: the flip is the heap, not the `my`.
GUARD: Pl/t/while-my-closure-01.t row 8 (fails on base).  Board: the four 105oneshot *PLAN* rows re-keyed #3493 -> #4643 (see the board header note s536d).
subject: NONDETERMINISTIC: IO-Compress t/105oneshot-{deflate,gzip,rawdeflate,zip}.t run 8 rows (the blessed 4 ok / 4 not ok, rc 2) OR stop after row 1 (rc 1) on the SAME tree, run to run -- a load-time `Carp::croak "NO!!!!"` in t/compress/CompTestUtils.pm LexFile::new: a fresh `my $name` argument arrives DEFINED
